7:1.sourceText: Ἐπειδὴ ἐπλήρωσεν πάντα τὰ ῥήματα αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς τοῦ λαοῦ, εἰσῆλθεν εἰς Καφαρναούμ.
7:1.targetText: When Jesus had concluded His discourse in the hearing of the people, He went to Capernaum.

groups.note: ῥήματα ("words, sayings") is rendered discourse.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB's "concluded His discourse" leaves πάντα ("all") without a separate word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb.

7:2.sourceText: Ἑκατοντάρχου δέ τινος δοῦλος κακῶς ἔχων ἤμελλεν τελευτᾶν, ὃς ἦν αὐτῷ ἔντιμος.
7:2.targetText: There a highly valued servant of a centurion was sick and about to die.

groups.note: ἔντιμος ("precious, honored") is rendered highly valued.
τινος ("a certain") is rendered a.
κακῶς ἔχων ("having it badly") means being sick.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts the account without rendering δέ.
BSB turns the relative clause ὃς ἦν αὐτῷ ("who was … to him") into the adjective "highly valued".

unmappedTarget.reason: English presentational opening with no Greek counterpart.
English joins the participle clause ("sick") to the main verb ἤμελλεν ("was about").

groups.note: The participle ἀκούσας ("having heard") is rendered as a When-clause.
τῶν Ἰουδαίων ("of the Jews") is rendered as the adjective Jewish.
The participle ἐρωτῶν ("asking") expresses the purpose of the sending.
ὅπως ("so that") with the subjunctive is rendered by the English infinitive.
διασώσῃ ("bring safely through") is rendered heal.

groups.note: οἱ … παραγενόμενοι ("those who had come") is rendered They came.

7:5.sourceText: ἀγαπᾷ γὰρ τὸ ἔθνος ἡμῶν καὶ τὴν συναγωγὴν αὐτὸς ᾠκοδόμησεν ἡμῖν.

7:6.targetText: So Jesus went with them. But when He was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends with the message: “Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy to have You come under my roof.

groups.note: The genitive absolute ἀπέχοντος ("being away") is rendered as a when-clause.
The participle λέγων ("saying") is rendered "with the message".

7:7.targetText: That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to You. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.

7:8.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπός εἰμι ὑπὸ ἐξουσίαν τασσόμενος, ἔχων ὑπ’ ἐμαυτὸν στρατιώτας, καὶ λέγω τούτῳ Πορεύθητι, καὶ πορεύεται, καὶ ἄλλῳ Ἔρχου, καὶ ἔρχεται, καὶ τῷ δούλῳ μου Ποίησον τοῦτο, καὶ ποιεῖ.
7:8.targetText: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes; and another to come, and he comes. I tell my servant to do something, and he does it.”

groups.note: καὶ ἐγώ ("I too, even I") is rendered "I myself" (as Matthew 8:9).

The reflexive ἐμαυτόν ("myself") is rendered me.
The one verb λέγω governs all three commands; BSB repeats it before the servant's command.
The dative τούτῳ ("to this one") is rendered one.
τοῦτο ("this") is rendered something and resumed as it (as Matthew 8:9).

7:9.sourceText: ἀκούσας δὲ ταῦτα ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐθαύμασεν αὐτόν, καὶ στραφεὶς τῷ ἀκολουθοῦντι αὐτῷ ὄχλῳ εἶπεν Λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐδὲ ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ τοσαύτην πίστιν εὗρον.

7:11.sourceText: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἑξῆς ἐπορεύθη εἰς πόλιν καλουμένην Ναΐν, καὶ συνεπορεύοντο αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλος πολύς.

groups.note: ἐν τῷ ἑξῆς ("in the next [time]") is rendered Soon afterward.
